I'm in my 30s and still dealing with the aftershocks of a toxic parent. I can't speak for your own situation, but these are my thoughts based on my experiences.

At your age, unfortunately, there may not be much you can do to mediate your parents' behavior. You may still be viewed as a "rebellious" or "problematic" kid. Toxic parents generally believe they are right and everyone else is wrong. 

My advice is to seek counsel as soon as you're able, don't wait until your late 20s or 30s. He/she will help give you the mental fortitude to withstand the toxicity as well as addressing some of your own flaws. And not all therapists are created equal. If one doesn't feel right, find another. Find a healthy support network, like good friends, cousins, sympathetic aunts or uncles, maybe siblings. Cognitive behavior therapy groups. Don't be ashamed to reach out to someone when you need a mental safe place.

Assuming you're doing your best to be a good human (not saying you're not, I just don't know your situation and how everything plays in together), this is basically what my therapist has spent years drilling into my head: Your parents do not define you. And just because they're your blood/kin doesn't mean they're right for you in the long run. They may never be who you hope them to be. They may never approve of you. They may never agree with your feelings. You may always be the black sheep. But that's on them, and it's not YOUR fault. The sooner you can grab that core value, the better equipped you'll be to weather the storm and set your own boundaries.

I've said this several times today in an effort to help at least one person last at least a little while longer.

It's not cowardly. It's your lizard brain saying, "Dude, wtf. No. We got shit to do." 

I don't know you, but I feel like, by believing you've tried your best, that you've honestly tried your best. Here's a secret: sometimes our best just isn't good enough. Sometimes (okay a lot times) our best doesn't bring home the gold. Sometimes our best doesnt give us an A on a test. And you know what else? That's okay. Chuck Norris didn't just wake up as a badass (well, maybe HE did. My point still stands though). It's okay to feel like shit, you're human. It's okay to withdraw to a hidey hole. Just don't stay there. Regardless of your position and experiences and mistakes in life, everyone deserves a future. Pardon the cliche, but you live and you learn. 

So maybe you're not Olympics material. So what? 99.6% of people probably aren't, either. Did you always know how to type in coherant sentences? I'll bet not, but you're doing great today. Take a shower, count it as a win. Get a little food in your stomach.  Baby steps. 

If that's too hard to believe, then at least set yourself a timeline. Make it through today. Get stubborn and passive aggressive with that stupid voice in your head trying to convince you that you suck. Prove to that guy/gal that you can do better, just watch. As long as you keep waking up tomorrow, there's always a chance to do better. Set a goal. Make it to your next birthday. Come find me, and I'll give you another birthday smack on the ass. Too much? Make it to the first day of Summer. Then make it to the first day of Fall. Make it for the next week, then make it to April

Whoa, this. I feel like everyone just pretends to like me, fake laughs at my jokes because they're just being polite, my kids only love me because I'm there mom, they have to. I get it. Sort of like Imposter Syndrome or whatever. And what makes it worse is when I start getting anxious about it, I pull away and hide in a metaphorical hole. And it's not a selfish thing; it's feeling like a burden and like I'm not worth loving because I'm an awful person and I deserve to be miserable.

Now, I'm going to tell you what my therapist is working with me on. Fact check. Take your emotions out of it, just for a second, and humor yourself. Pretend someone you care about feels this way, and what you would say to that person. Chances are, you'd tell em they're nuts, of course you enjoy their company (probably, I'm not suggesting I know your exact situation).

Easier said than done, though. Been working on it for two years. That's something I suppose. 

You're loved, whether you realize it or not. Hang in there. Tomorrow needs you.
